```luau
-- No requires, no side effects. Returns { list = {...}, byId = {...}, ores = {...} }.
--
-- BUDGET MATH (a full tree takes about 8-10 minutes)
--   Total cost of all 10 upgrades:
--     10 + 30 + 60 + 100 + 200 + 350 + 500 + 800 + 1500 + 2500 = 6050 cash
--   Base income is 1 dropper x 1 cash / 2 s = 0.5 cash/s. The first buy (10) is covered by a
--   small starter grant / early income so it lands within ~10 s of claiming a plot.
--   Income after each milestone (cubes per 2 s cycle x ore value x cash multiplier, per second):
--     dropper2                    2 x 1 x 1.0 / 2 =  1.0 /s
--     tier_silver                 2 x 3 x 1.0 / 2 =  3.0 /s
--     dropper3                    3 x 3 x 1.0 / 2 =  4.5 /s
--     mult1 (x1.5)                3 x 3 x 1.5 / 2 =  6.75/s
--     tier_gold                   3 x 8 x 1.5 / 2 = 18   /s
--     dropper4                    4 x 8 x 1.5 / 2 = 24   /s
--     mult2 (x2)                  4 x 8 x 2.0 / 2 = 32   /s
--     tier_diamond                4 x 20 x 2.0 / 2 = 80  /s
--   (speed upgrades only shorten the trip to the collector; they raise throughput of cubes
--   in flight, not value per cube.) Rough timeline: ~20 s to dropper2 + silver (40 cash),
--   ~60 s to speed1 + dropper3, ~2 min for mult1, ~3.5 min for gold, ~5 min for speed2 and
--   dropper4, ~7 min for mult2, and ~8-10 min for diamond (2500 at ~32/s plus pacing and
--   walking between pads). Players who skip around the tree finish slightly faster or slower,
--   but the tail cost (mult2 + diamond = 4000 of 6050) keeps the full tree near 8-10 minutes.
--
-- Effect shapes:
--   { kind = "dropper",  slots = n }   total active dropper slots after purchase
--   { kind = "tier",     tier = n }    ore tier every dropper spits out (index into ores)
--   { kind = "speed",    mult = x }    conveyor speed multiplier
--   { kind = "cashMult", mult = x }    collector cash multiplier

local list = {
	{ id = "dropper2", name = "Dropper 2", cost = 10, requires = nil, effect = { kind = "dropper", slots = 2 } },
	{ id = "tier_silver", name = "Silver Ore", cost = 30, requires = "dropper2", effect = { kind = "tier", tier = 2 } },
	{ id = "speed1", name = "Speed 1", cost = 60, requires = "dropper2", effect = { kind = "speed", mult = 1.5 } },
	{ id = "dropper3", name = "Dropper 3", cost = 100, requires = "dropper2", effect = { kind = "dropper", slots = 3 } },
	{ id = "mult1", name = "Cash x1.5", cost = 200, requires = "tier_silver", effect = { kind = "cashMult", mult = 1.5 } },
	{ id = "tier_gold", name = "Gold Ore", cost = 350, requires = "tier_silver", effect = { kind = "tier", tier = 3 } },
	{ id = "speed2", name = "Speed 2", cost = 500, requires = "speed1", effect = { kind = "speed", mult = 2 } },
	{ id = "dropper4", name = "Dropper 4", cost = 800, requires = "dropper3", effect = { kind = "dropper", slots = 4 } },
	{ id = "mult2", name = "Cash x2", cost = 1500, requires = "mult1", effect = { kind = "cashMult", mult = 2 } },
	{ id = "tier_diamond", name = "Diamond Ore", cost = 2500, requires = "tier_gold", effect = { kind = "tier", tier = 4 } },
}

-- Indexed by tier.
local ores = {
	{ name = "Bronze", value = 1, color = Color3.fromRGB(205, 127, 50), material = Enum.Material.Metal, sparkles = false },
	{ name = "Silver", value = 3, color = Color3.fromRGB(205, 210, 220), material = Enum.Material.Metal, sparkles = false },
	{ name = "Gold", value = 8, color = Color3.fromRGB(255, 205, 40), material = Enum.Material.Foil, sparkles = false },
	{ name = "Diamond", value = 20, color = Color3.fromRGB(80, 235, 255), material = Enum.Material.Glass, sparkles = true },
}

local byId = {}
for _, upgrade in ipairs(list) do
	byId[upgrade.id] = upgrade
end

return {
	list = list,
	byId = byId,
	ores = ores,
}

```

Playtest critique:
- The first buy relies on early income, but cubes_collected never rose, so Dropper 2 cannot be afforded. The tutorial is stuck at step 1 and nobody gets guided to the pad. (hint: Raise the starter cash so the first upgrade is affordable at once (the upgrades are priced from $10). # Lessons
## Design
- Tune early progression so a playtest of roughly 15 seconds can reach the first purchase or milestone. Use a fast starting income or a cheap first upgrade (a few seconds of income). Slow openings leave the buy loop untested and feel dull.
- Give per-event feedback for every economy action: a "+N" popup on collect, plus HUD hints for upgrade cost, affordability or progress. Without it, numbers going up feels weak between purchases.
- Place trigger pads (buy pads, claim gates, etc.) off the spawn path so walking from spawn never fires them accidentally.
- Make moving cubes or other spawned items non-colliding with players (CanCollide = false, or a collision group) and cap their count per area. Otherwise they jitter, stick or knock players around.
- Keep the time to first core-loop activity well inside the playtest window (the probe may last only ~10-15s). Any auto-claim or auto-start fallback should fire within a few seconds (about 3-5s, not 20s), and claim gates should sit near the spawn area, not far outside the plaza. An idle player must still reach the loop quickly.
- Keep tutorial text consistent with the actual flow (e.g. don't say "walk to a gate" if auto-claim happens within seconds). Tutorial steps must be advanced by events that actually occur, or the player is left without guidance.
